facts.value: To convey communicative and intercultural foreign language skills, refresh and complete existing basic knowledge in English, and impart subject-specific vocabulary along with an introduction to general aspects of the economy in English-speaking countries.
Three levels: FOUNDATION, KEYSTONE, and HIGHER.
FOUNDATION level consists of course WE1A. All Foundation courses have the same level of difficulty (goal level B1.2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) and content.
Completion of level A2/B1 of the GER or 26 – 40 points in the placement test.
It is recommended to take the placement test before registration to ensure proper course placement.

In the Business English Foundation course, students learn vocabulary and expressions specifically for the business world. Various exercises should promote linguistic and conceptual understanding of current topics and provide a basis for discussions and written exercises on various economic topics. The reading and writing portion of the course is assessed in a 90-minute written exam during the last week of the semester. A graded certificate is issued for passing the exam.
Unit 1 – What is Economics? Unit 2 – Economic Indicators Unit 3 – Economic Cycle Unit 4 – Retail Banking Unit 5 – Retail.
For all levels, students receive working materials with exercises designed specifically for students of economics and selected economic texts.
90 Euros for WE1A Foundation (13 double hours, including the final exam).

KEYSTONE level consists of parallel courses WE2A – WE2D. All Keystone courses have the same level of difficulty (goal level B2.1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) and content.
Completion of level B1 of the GER or 41 – 60 points in the placement test.

In the Business English Keystone course, students learn vocabulary and expressions specifically for the business world. Various exercises should promote linguistic and conceptual understanding of current topics and provide a basis for discussions and written exercises on various economic topics. The reading and writing portion of the course is assessed in a 90-minute written exam during the last week of the semester. A graded certificate is issued for passing the exam.
Unit 1 – Start-ups Unit 2 – The 'Gig Economy' Unit 3 – Economic Cycle Unit 4 – Economic Theory in Practice Unit 5 – Fintech.
90 Euros for WE2A, WE2B, WE2C, and WE2D Keystone (13 double hours, including the final exam).

HIGHER level consists of parallel courses WE3A – WE3D. All Higher courses have the same level of difficulty (goal level B2.2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) and content.
Completion of level B2.1 of the GER or 61 – 80 points in the placement test.

In the Business English Higher course, students learn vocabulary and expressions specifically for the business world. Various exercises should promote linguistic and conceptual understanding of current topics and provide a basis for discussions and written exercises on various economic topics. The reading and writing portion of the course is assessed in a 90-minute written exam during the last week of the semester. A graded certificate is issued for passing the exam.
Unit 1 – Future of Work Unit 2 – Economic Migration Unit 3 – Poverty Unit 4 – Philanthropy Unit 5 – Tax Evasion and Tax Avoidance.
90 Euros for WE3A, WE3B, WE3C, and WE3D Higher (13 double hours, including the final exam).
For all levels, students receive working materials with exercises designed specifically for students of economics and selected economic texts.
